subject: Aurelia PoC — post-demo model shortlist & proposed sprint plan
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aureliadata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Aurelia PoC — post-demo model shortlist & proposed sprint plan

Jordan — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

TL;DR (recommended path)
- Shortlist three candidate model configurations for the PoC (below).
- Redwood to run a focused eval on your sample prompt set (attached) and share cost/latency estimates for 3x throughput scenarios.
- If results look good, set a 2-week PoC with a canary rollout and automated quality checks we define together.

What we saw in the demo
- Good baseline fidelity on shorter prompts (~<300 tokens).
- Two failure modes to watch: named-entity hallucinations on long context and occasional verbosity on multi-turn follow-ups.

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs at a glance)
1) redwood-small-1.0-q4 — ultra-low cost, sub-100ms p95 at typical lengths; lower instruction-following fidelity on longer legalese.
2) redwood-mid-2.7-q4_k — balanced: ~2-3x cost of small, better adherence and fewer hallucinations for prompts up to 1k tokens.
3) redwood-large-6.9-pt — highest quality, best on tricky multi-turn contexts; cost & latency higher; recommended for narrow-production paths where quality is the priority.

Attached: prompt set v1, initial benchmark CSV, and a concise cost/latency table. We ran these with your sample dataset (thanks for sharing). See the Drive link I’ve included in metadata for the full run.

Next steps proposed
- Our team runs the focused eval (2 business days) and returns a short report with: accuracy by intent, hallucination examples, per-model cost/latency estimates for your 3 throughput targets (10TPS steady / 50TPS peak / 200TPS burst).
- We align on canary metrics and rollback thresholds (quality thresholds, latency SLOs).
- If you approve, we provision a reserved PoC environment and support a 2-week run with daily syncs.

Can you confirm:
- Decision criteria that matter most (e.g., max cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency target, allowed hallucination rate), and
- Who should be on the PoC daily syncs (engineering, ML, product)?

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Connor — thanks for the crisp recap. A few quick answers: 

Decision criteria (ranked):
1) Precision on entity extraction (we can tolerate lower recall but not false attributions)
2) Max p95 latency 250ms for our 10TPS steady workload
3) Monthly spend target for PoC <$7k (approx)

Participants for daily syncs: myself (product), Maya (ML lead — maya.srinivasan@aureliadata.com), and Viktor (platform). I’ll add them to a calendar invite after you confirm cadence.

Please prioritize: the per-model hallucination examples and parity against our entity extraction baseline. Also send any suggested prompt-engineering quick wins we can try in the PoC.

Appreciate it — Jordan
Jordan Price
Product Lead, Aurelia Data
jordan.price@aureliadata.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aureliadata.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia PoC — post-demo model shortlist & proposed sprint plan (benchmarks + notes)

Jordan / Connor — attaching the initial runs and a short interpretation. Key notes below; full CSV is attached and in Drive.

Benchmarks summary (sample-based; 1k prompt subset):
- redwood-small-1.0-q4: mean latency 32ms, p95 78ms; token cost ~$0.0018 per request (avg prompt). Entity precision 0.83, recall 0.70. Hallucination examples concentrated on long-context (>=800 tokens).
- redwood-mid-2.7-q4_k: mean latency 110ms, p95 245ms; token cost ~$0.0056 per request. Entity precision 0.92, recall 0.86. Hallucination rate dropped ~60% vs small.
- redwood-large-6.9-pt: mean latency 360ms, p95 520ms; token cost ~$0.018 per request. Entity precision 0.96, recall 0.91. Lowest hallucinations but occasional verbosity produced spurious qualifiers.

Quality regression concerns and mitigations:
- Observed instability for prompts that include noisy OCR artifacts — recommend a light pre-clean step in the pipeline before sending context.
- Models show divergent behavior on embedded tables in-context — for the PoC we suggest converting tables to structured JSON snippets when possible.
- Canary checks: (1) automated entity-precision scoring on a holdout set; (2) daily spot checks for hallucination cases; (3) a human-in-the-loop threshold if precision falls below 0.88 for two consecutive days.

Prompt-engineering quick wins to include in PoC:
- Prefer explicit instructions: e.g., "Return only the following fields: name, date_of_birth, account_id. Do not introduce new entities."
- Use a short system-level instruction for role context and a separate user instruction for the extraction fields.
- If token budgets are tight, shard longer docs into 400–600 token windows and merge outputs via a consolidation step.

Recommendation for PoC configuration (proposed):
- Start canary on redwood-mid-2.7-q4_k for the first 2 business days (best balance). If precision is >=0.90 and p95 <= 250ms, move to a 1-week split test with redwood-small-1.0-q4 for throughput validation. Reserve redwood-large-6.9-pt as a failover for high-criticality routes.

Deliverables we will return in 48 hours:
- Updated benchmark CSV with labeled hallucination cases and contextual examples.
- Prompt set v1 (attached) + 3 alternate engineering variants.
- Cost scenarios for 10/50/200 TPS.

Connor — I’ll coordinate the test harness and can spin the canary env once we have your sign-off and an approved billing contact.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
